method: First-to-last inert source reading; static mathematical/code-path analysis; original-byte hashing and metadata comparison. No supplied execution/import/compilation/syntax parsing/test runs. Reviewer-authored JSON/hash/report packaging only.

rows.mathematical_scope: Lines 8–32 construct an m=N/2 quadratic-chirp Hankel matrix over a field with a primitive 2N-th root. The diagonal–Vandermonde factorization is algebraically correct: (a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2ab and omega=xi^2. Distinct evaluation points give rank m. Lines 35–61 check the separated half-cut of a sum of q diagonal-gauged inverse path-tridiagonals with one common path order. A common-order cut has rank at most q, while the Fourier consecutive-row/consecutive-column cut is Vandermonde of rank m. These are architecture-specific additive barriers.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept the exact identity and common-order additive rank argument within the stated model. Do not generalize it to arbitrary Fourier algorithms, different path orders, products, or a runtime speedup.

rows.mathematical_scope: The 459-line module supplies finite-field primality/root search, exact Gaussian rank, monotone and balanced separation witnesses, tridiagonal solves and cut extraction, determinant polynomials, prime- and power-of-two Fourier cut certificates, a noncommutativity witness, and adversarial separation controls. For powers of two, reduction modulo X^(N/2)+1 is exactly the cyclotomic reduction. For prime N and determinant size at least 2, the coefficient sum at X=1 vanishes, so a nonzero reduced degree<N polynomial cannot be a nonzero multiple of Phi_N. Balanced separation preserves earlier separations by taking subsets and retains at least half of each color at every new order. The complex Fourier cut rank bound is rank(F[R,C])>=|R||C|/N, from Frobenius norm and operator norm of normalized Fourier submatrices. With m²>qN this excludes sums of q separated inverse-tridiagonal cuts, regardless of sampled Green coefficients.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept the finite-field and algebraic witness machinery subject to its domains, and the separated-cut proof within the additive architecture. No execution result is certified by this read; no general FFT lower bound follows.

rows.mathematical_scope: Implements the finite-field dyadic frequency folding R and its inverse, plus inverse residual A through unfolding followed by inverse B-FFTs. Per level, high/other=(u+tw·v,u-tw·v), and inverse uses (high+other)/2 and (high-other)/(2tw). This algebra is correct when all intended slots/groups are present. The complex Gram identity in the docstring is not computed by this modular implementation.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept the finite-field inverse formulas within canonical valid phase15 parameters and groups. Complex unitarity and large-size execution need separate evidence.

rows.mathematical_scope: Full 249-line exact positive-sign finite-field Fourier executor for powers of two with 8<=B<N<=B², L=N/B. It builds L independent B-point FFTs, folds even frequencies by dyadic butterflies, gathers residual rows according to multiplication-by-(1+B) orbits, then performs orbit FFTs with phase factors. The displayed geometric-sum formula supports the sparse residual oracle. The final count is exactly N log2(N)/2 butterflies; source explicitly says no speedup. The finite field has 2-power roots only through 2^23.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept as an auditable finite-field folded FFT design with conserved classical work, subject to canonical helper inputs. No tests, import, compilation or actual transform evaluation were performed here.

rows.mathematical_scope: The support theorem is valid for the stated model: if F=M_t B_t^-1 ... B_1^-1 M_0 and each B_i has at most s nonzeros per row while M_i are monomial, then F^-1 has row support at most s^t. A dense inverse Fourier matrix requires s^t>=N. The integer loop computes ceil(log_s N) without floating logarithms. The random routine tracks Boolean possible support, so numerical cancellations cannot invalidate its upper bound.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept the sparse-inverse product support argument and small valid-domain Boolean controls. Repair input guards before treating the random helper as a general callable audit.

rows.mathematical_scope: Exact finite-field entrywise Fourier covariance falsification: positive-sign F has FZ=DF, with Ze_j=e_(j+1). It compares every entry of a sampled modular stage and separately counts deviations of its first column from all ones. Covariance plus the all-ones first column uniquely determines the unnormalized Fourier matrix; covariance alone permits arbitrary row scaling, including zero rows.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept exact finite-instance covariance calculation design. Require dimensions, field embedding and inspected output counts for any actual rejection claim.

rows.mathematical_scope: Exact fixed-instance covariance-rank correction bound. If S+E intertwines Z,D then SZ-DS=-(EZ-DE), so rank(SZ-DS)<=rank(EZ)+rank(DE)<=2 rank(E). Thus any correction has rank at least ceil(r/2). This bound concerns additive corrections to the fixed stage, not stage products, and the source states that boundary.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept the rank inequality and prescribed modular-instance calculation. Preserve field/dependency identity and one-stage additive-correction scope.

rows.mathematical_scope: Computes analytic l_p operator-norm upper bounds for a fixed-strength phase12 architecture. general bound 1+2/(1-d|alpha|delta) requires p in [1,2], delta=2/p-1 and d|alpha|delta<1. Path bound uses a stronger l1 Neumann bound interpolated with l2 unitarity. Combining path² and normalized I+i epsilon R yields K. A normalized Fourier matrix has l_p norm N^(1/p-1/2), giving t>=log(N^(1/p-1/2))/log K for products of these fixed stages and l_p-isometric interleavings. The helper does not prove the cited analytic interpolation/resolvent steps; they are assumptions/theoretical derivation, not numerical fitting.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept the conditional analytic norm-budget argument. Treat numeric rounded stage counts as ordinary floating estimates until certified; retain architecture/parameter restrictions.

rows.mathematical_scope: Necessary two-stage invariant: if A=S2 Q P S1 satisfies AZ=DA, then Q P (S1 Z S1^-1) P^-1 Q^-1=S2^-1 D S2. Diagonal similarity leaves diagonal entries unchanged, and permutation similarity permutes them, so the diagonal multisets must match. A mismatch excludes every intermediate permutation and invertible diagonal for these fixed S1,S2 in the chosen field; equality is not sufficient. The two component formulas correctly compute diagonal entries of the conjugates.
rows.acceptance_boundary: Accept the exact necessary invariant and fixed-instance veto methodology within field/root/inverse assumptions. A matching multiset never certifies successful synthesis.
